title: control-plane-resources-crud-api-sketch
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a first-pass data model and CRUD API surface for the control plane objects used by runtime routing and multi-region deployments. Focus is pragmatic: minimal canonical fields to support routing policies, environment scoping, region/cluster awareness, versioned rollouts, and safe updates in distributed stores.

High level goals:
- Canonical resource model that is small and expressive for routing decisions (policy evaluation at request-time).
- CRUD APIs with optimistic concurrency and audit trails for safe rollouts.
- Multi-region-friendly: clear primary/replica semantics, eventual consistency tradeoffs documented.
- Support for canary/blue-green rollouts and routing weights.

Key concepts and objects (vocab):
- Resource: generic top-level entity that routing policies target (e.g., model-route, serving-route, bucket). Resources are namespaced under an Environment.
- Environment: logical isolation boundary (dev/staging/prod or customer-specific).
- Region: physical geography (us-west1, eu-central1).
- Cluster: a serving cluster within a region (e.g., cluster-gpu-01). Clusters belong to Regions and are selectable by routing policies.
- Route: compiled policy applied to incoming requests; references resources, model variants, clusters, weights, priorities.
- Revision: immutable snapshot/version of a resource used for rollouts (resource -> revisions[]).

Data model (flat field lists for each primary object):
1) Environment
- id (string, dns-friendly)
- name (human)
- owner_team (string)
- created_at (ISO8601)
- updated_at (ISO8601)
- tags (string[])
- region_affinity (string[] optional) -- preferred regions for resources created in this env

2) Cluster
- id (string)
- region (string)
- capacity_units (int approximate as string e.g. "128-gpu-cores")
- labels (string[] key=value)
- status (string: active|draining|offline)
- maintenance_window (string freeform)
- created_at, updated_at

3) Resource (generic)
- id (string) // unique within environment
- environment_id (string)
- kind (string) // e.g., "model-route", "ingress-policy"
- spec (string) // opaque JSON blob stored as text (see spec shape examples below)
- current_revision_id (string) // points to latest active revision
- revisions (string[]) // ordered list of revision ids
- owner (string)
- tags (string[])
- lifecycle_state (string: active|deprecated|disabled)
- created_at, updated_at

4) Revision
- id (string)
- resource_id (string)
- author (string)
- spec (string) // immutable snapshot text
- created_at

Routing policy (spec example as stored in Resource.spec):
- policy_type: "route-v1"
- match: {prefix: "/v1/generate", headers: [{name: "x-tenant", type: "exact"}] }
- rules: [ {id: "r1", priority: 10, targets: [{cluster_selector: "gpu-*-west", weight: 70, model_variant: "m-4bit"}, {cluster_selector: "cpu-*-eu", weight: 30, model_variant: "m-quant"}], fallback: {cluster_selector: "default"} } ]
- evaluation_options: {prefer_local_region: true, respect_client_region_hint: true}
- rollout: {type: "canary", stages: [{revision: "rev-2026-03-01-1", traffic_percent: 5, start_at: "2026-03-05T00:00:00Z"}, {revision: "rev-2026-03-01-2", traffic_percent: 100, start_after: "P1D"}]}

Notes on spec storage: spec is stored as an opaque string in the Resource to keep the control plane schema flexible. We validate via JSON Schema server-side and generate Revision snapshots on update.

CRUD API surface (REST patterns):
Base: https://api.redwood.internal/controlplane/v1
- Create Environment: POST /environments
  payload: {"id":"prod","name":"Production","owner_team":"core-ai","region_affinity":["us-west1","us-east1"]}
  returns 201 with environment object and ETag header for concurrency.

- Get Environment: GET /environments/{env_id}
- List Environments: GET /environments?owner_team=core-ai
- Update Environment (partial): PATCH /environments/{env_id} with If-Match: <etag> header
- Delete Environment: DELETE /environments/{env_id} (soft-delete; marks lifecycle_state=disabled)

- Create Resource: POST /environments/{env_id}/resources
  payload: {"id":"route-oai-gen","kind":"model-route","spec": "{...}", "owner":"prod-pm"}
  returns 201, creates initial Revision, returns revision_id and etag

- Get Resource: GET /environments/{env_id}/resources/{res_id}
  query params: ?revision=rev-id to fetch immutable snapshot
- List Resources: GET /environments/{env_id}/resources?kind=model-route&tag=beta
- Update Resource (full replace): PUT /environments/{env_id}/resources/{res_id} with If-Match: <etag>
  semantics: validate new spec, create new Revision, advance current_revision_id on successful commit
- Patch Resource (merge): PATCH with JSON Merge Patch semantics; creates Revision if spec changed
- Delete Resource: DELETE /environments/{env_id}/resources/{res_id} (soft-delete; resource remains for history and audits)

- Revisions: GET /environments/{env_id}/resources/{res_id}/revisions
- Rollback: POST /environments/{env_id}/resources/{res_id}/rollback body: {"revision_id":"rev-2026-02-20-3"} -> creates new revision that re-applies snapshot and increments revision history

Optimistic concurrency and ETags:
- All mutable object reads return ETag header (hash of canonical fields + spec)
- Updates require If-Match header; service returns 412 if mismatch.
- For long-lived UIs, we provide a lightweight watch API (see events below) to reduce collision frequency.

Multi-region semantics and replication strategy:
- Primary region: control-plane writes are directed to a primary region per environment (configured on Environment.region_affinity[0]) when strong ordering is needed (e.g., environment creation).
- Async replicas: other regions replicate via write-ahead-event-streams; propagation typically seconds to tens of seconds.
- Reads: reads can be served from local replica for low latency; for strongly-consistent operations (e.g., evaluate rollout completion) callers must request ?read_consistency=strong which routes to primary.
- Conflict resolution: updates are linearized via primary or resolved with MVCC using revision ids. In rare cross-primary failover scenarios we apply last-writer-wins by timestamp + author id, but prefer controlled failover procedures.

Routing policy evaluation notes (runtime):
- The serving runtime consumes compiled routes (materialized from Resource.current_revision) pushed via an event bus to clusters.
- Runtime key inputs: incoming request headers, client region hint, model availability matrix (cluster -> model variant mapping), current cluster load.
- The evaluation result is: target cluster id(s), model variant id, reason (e.g., weight-split, fallback).

Observability and auditability:
- Every control-plane mutation emits an event: {entity, operation, actor, before_rev, after_rev, timestamp}. These are stored in an append-only event log (for replication, audit, and to drive runtime delta pushes).
- Audit UI queries events with filters by actor, resource, time range.

Operational considerations / open questions:
- Spec size limits: cap Resource.spec at 64KB to avoid shipping heavy payloads to runtime. Large policies -> reference external named policy objects.
- ACLs: currently ACLs are at Environment-level. Need finer-grained RBAC for resource-level approvals and code-owner style guardrails.
- Garbage collection: Deleted resources keep history for 90 days; then tombstone + archive to cold storage.
- Rate limits: control-plane write throttling per environment to avoid noisy CI/CD loops causing constant rollouts.

Examples (curl):
- Create resource:
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/controlplane/v1/environments/prod/resources" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" -d '{"id":"route-summarize","kind":"model-route","spec":"{\"policy_type\":\"route-v1\",\"rules\":[]}","owner":"runtime"}'

- Patch resource (merge):
  curl -X PATCH -H "If-Match: "$ETAG"" "https://api.redwood.internal/controlplane/v1/environments/prod/resources/route-summarize" -d '{"spec":"{...updated...}"}'

Wrap-up / next steps:
- Iterate this sketch into a concise OpenAPI spec and JSON Schemas for Resource.spec variants (route-v1, security-policy-v1).
- Implement a small prototype service (single-primary region) and a push pipeline to a mock cluster to validate latency and replication window.
- Design RBAC matrix and finalize ETag algorithm (SHA256 over ordered fields).

Notes to reviewers: look particularly at the spec storage tradeoff (opaque string vs typed DB columns) and the multi-region read_consistency option. Feedback on rollout semantics and API ergonomics would be most helpful.
